summary: Lovastatin is an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor that lowers LDL-C and reduces coronary heart disease risk. It is taken with the evening meal, usually 20-40 mg daily (range 10-80 mg). It is a CYP3A4 substrate with notable interactions; key risks are myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Contraindicated in active liver disease and pregnancy.
indications: Primary prevention of coronary heart disease in patients without symptomatic CVD with elevated total-C/LDL-C and below-average HDL-C
Reduce elevated total-C and LDL-C in primary hypercholesterolemia (Fredrickson types IIa and IIb)
Slow progression of coronary atherosclerosis in patients with coronary heart disease
Adolescent patients (10-17 years) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia
Adjunct to diet for hypertriglyceridemia and dysbetalipoproteinemia

dosage.d: Start 20 mg once daily with evening meal; range 10-80 mg/day
dosage.t: Once daily (or BID for higher doses)
dosage.n: Start 10 mg if modest LDL reduction needed

dosage.d: Up to 80 mg/day in single or two divided doses
dosage.n: Max 80 mg/day; see interaction dose caps

dosage.d: Doses above 20 mg/day only with caution
Limit dose (e.g., max 20 mg with amiodarone; 40 mg with diltiazem/verapamil)

admin: Take orally with the evening meal; food enhances absorption
Higher doses (e.g., 80 mg) may be divided into morning and evening doses
Maintain a standard cholesterol-lowering diet before and during therapy
Observe dose limits when combined with interacting drugs (amiodarone, verapamil, diltiazem, etc.)
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and large amounts of grapefruit juice
moa: Lovastatin is a prodrug hydrolyzed to its active beta-hydroxyacid form, which competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in hepatic cholesterol synthesis. Reduced intracellular cholesterol upregulates hepatic LDL receptors, increasing LDL clearance and lowering plasma LDL-C, total cholesterol and triglycerides.

absolute: Active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations
Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, nefazodone)
relative: Predisposition to myopathy (advanced age, hypothyroidism, debilitation)

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Cholesterol biosynthesis is important for fetal development; discontinue lovastatin when pregnancy is recognized. Advise effective contraception in women of childbearing potential.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding. A small amount of another statin is excreted in human milk; because of potential serious adverse effects in the infant, women taking lovastatin should not breastfeed.
renal: Use caution and titrate carefully in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min); doses above 20 mg/day should be used only when clearly needed because myopathy risk rises.
hepatic: Contraindicated in active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations. Use cautiously in patients who consume substantial alcohol or have a history of liver disease.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (itraconazole, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, erythromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, nefazodone, cobicistat) - contraindicated, marked myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk
Cyclosporine, gemfibrozil, danazol - avoid or contraindicated
moderate: Verapamil, diltiazem - limit lovastatin to 40 mg/day
Other fibrates and niacin (>=1 g/day) - increased myopathy risk
interactions.food: Take with food (improves bioavailability); avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice (raises levels).
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; heavy use increases hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate transaminases and creatine kinase.

emergency: Rhabdomyolysis (severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine)

monitoring: Lipid panel at baseline and 4-12 weeks after initiation or dose change
Liver enzymes at baseline and as clinically indicated
Creatine kinase if unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness
counsel: Report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness promptly
Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice and limit alcohol
Tell your doctor about all medicines - some antibiotics, antifungals and heart drugs interact
Do not take if pregnant or breastfeeding; use reliable contraception
pk: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F), protect from light
pearls: Prodrug activated to its beta-hydroxyacid; CYP3A4 substrate with many interactions
Contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; dose caps with amiodarone (20 mg), diltiazem/verapamil (40 mg)
Lower potency than atorvastatin/rosuvastatin; best taken with the evening meal
Avoid in active liver disease and pregnancy
Monitor for and counsel about muscle symptoms; rhabdomyolysis is rare but serious
missed: Take the missed dose with food when remembered, unless it is close to the next dose; then skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: No specific treatment; few cases reported with full recovery. Treat symptomatically and supportively, and monitor for hepatic and muscle effects. Due to extensive protein binding, hemodialysis is not expected to enhance clearance.
